title: Go versions come from tags, and a dependent follows the library
prompt: We want to cut a release for our two Go modules. The engine picked up a `Normalize` helper since the last release. Get monochange set up so it can plan versions for these modules and record that change, then show me what would ship. Note that Go doesn't carry a version inside the module file.
expectation: Go modules carry no package version in go.mod. With tag = true, monochange resolves their release baselines from tags matching each owner's version_format; initial_version is needed only as a fallback when a matching tag does not exist. This fixture already provides core/v1.2.0 and service/v1.0.0 tags, so planning must use that history. Preparing the release rewrites the service's internal require to the released core version while preserving local replace directives. Package ids may be chosen by the agent, but rendered submodule tags must retain the existing core/v and service/v namespaces; changing ids must not silently reset those baselines to initial_version.
setupCommands: git init -b main -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm init && git tag core/v1.2.0 && git tag service/v1.0.0

checks.command: node -e 'const assert=require("node:assert/strict");const {spawnSync}=require("node:child_process");const path=require("node:path");const cli=args=>{const r=spawnSync("monochange",args,{encoding:"utf8"});assert.equal(r.status,0,r.stderr);return JSON.parse(r.stdout);};const c=cli(["config","--format","json"]).config;const byPath=new Map(c.packages.map(p=>[path.normalize(p.path),p]));const core=byPath.get("core");const service=byPath.get("service");assert.ok(core);assert.ok(service);assert.equal(core.package_type,"go");assert.equal(service.package_type,"go");'
checks.why: Resolve each Go module by its configured directory, allowing valid user-chosen release ids.

checks.command: node -e 'const assert=require("node:assert/strict");const {spawnSync}=require("node:child_process");const path=require("node:path");const cli=args=>{const r=spawnSync("monochange",args,{encoding:"utf8"});assert.equal(r.status,0,r.stderr);return JSON.parse(r.stdout);};const c=cli(["config","--format","json"]).config;const byPath=new Map(c.packages.map(p=>[path.normalize(p.path),p]));const core=byPath.get("core");const service=byPath.get("service");assert.ok(core);assert.ok(service);const d=cli(["preview","--format","json"]);const targets=new Map(d.release_targets.map(t=>[t.id,t]));assert.equal(targets.get(core.id)?.version,"1.3.0");assert.equal(targets.get(service.id)?.version,"1.0.1");assert.equal(targets.get(core.id)?.tag_name,"core/v1.3.0");assert.equal(targets.get(service.id)?.tag_name,"service/v1.0.1");'
checks.why: Both requested versions must be planned under the existing Go submodule tag namespaces, so their baselines continue to resolve from the seeded release history.
Go has no manifest version field, and inventing one produces a file the toolchain rejects. This is the misconception the scenario is built to catch.
The service depends on the engine, so preparation must update its require directive to the newly released core version rather than retain the old dependency reference.
The replace is a local development override. Rewriting it would break the workspace layout the modules depend on.
The request was to plan a release and show what would ship, not to publish or push tags.
